emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(rcu_state.n_force_qs)]) from thread_a (the global counter sample compared against rdp->n_force_qs_snap must be single-copy)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@rcu_gp_fqs:1910 = WRITE(rcu_state.n_force_qs++) by the grace-period kthread
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the enqueue reader holds no lock covering this global counter, and the GP-kthread increment is not serialized with it -> no common lock/order for this field
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent (non-atomic increment) write -> data race on a heuristic counter

fix_maps_to: patch marks the increment WRITE_ONCE(rcu_state.n_force_qs, rcu_state.n_force_qs + 1) and all snapshot reads READ_ONCE -> single-copy atomicity only; NO exclusion/order added (the comparison stays a lockless heuristic) -> atomic([read]) at the access-marking level
recall_risk_notes: Benign heuristic counter (commit: 'these data races are hard to make happen'); required_ordering = 'use marked accesses'. The read only drives an optimization (whether to kick the grace period), so the arbiter would likely reject the atomic(read) assume as a real correctness requirement -> FN. The conflict pair itself is easy to find: the object (global rcu_state.n_force_qs) is trivial and the two entries (call_rcu vs rcu_gp_kthread) are distinct.
